newsitem.title: KENYA: Power monopoly stocks in rally at Nairobi bourse. [corrected 13:37 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Power monopoly stocks in rally at Nairobi bourse. [corrected 13:37 gmt]

text.p: Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting Co staged a dramatic rally at the Nairobi Stock Exchange gaining 161 shillings to close at 335 on Friday.
The rally was partly based on the company's announcement of a doubled dividend and bonus issue from last year.
The 20-share index jumped 154.67 points to stand at 3550.27. Turnover was posted at 19.197 million shillings on 692,017 shares from 19.582 million shillings traded on 441,369 shares.

On Thursday a broker from leading stock brokerage firm Shah, Munge & Partners said they had placed some 44,000 Kenya Power & Lighting Co shares on offer at 500 -- "just to see how far the price could go".
The company has announced a final dividend of eight shillings and a bonus of two shares for every one held.
"At 335 the share is still a very good buy because after the books close and the share trades ex-price, it should have a fair value of 166 which is still high," a senior broker said.
A large number of market players admitted that the share's rally caught them by surprise but thought that the buying euphoria could have been trigerred by a leak of the results.

Bourse officials and brokers said a wave of buying pressure had caught on at the market but could not be matched by supply as most investors were holding onto their shares in anticipation of good end-year results expected anytime between end February.
Oil concern Total Kenya gained 10 to 82 and British American Tobacco Kenya rose 2.0 to 70.50.

"Last year released dividends thrice in the year but it has now reverted to the final and interim system and so investors are hoping to earn a bigger dividend because it should be consolidated," a senior broker said.

On average, the market maintained its bullish tone with prices of key shares registering marginal gains. Barclays Bank gained 3.0 to close at 122 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 60 from 57.50.
Some 300,000 shares of Kenya Airways traded on the three-day special board at a reserve price of 10.50 from 10.15 changed hands between foreigners.
Brooke Bond dropped to 150 from 154 while Sasini Tea & Coffee was unchanged at 66 while Kazuki edged higher to 98 from 97.50. (Corrects Sasini price.)
Bourse officials and brokers said the apparent price drop in Brooke Bond was a corrective measure because the share had been trading at an overvalued price.
